question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The head coach declared that the player who will score the most points in the game will clinch the trophy this year.
option_2: who were score the maximum points
option_3: who have score the maximum points
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. who scores the maximum points.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a sentence with a future main clause and a subordinate clause of condition/time introduced by a relative pronoun, the subordinate clause takes the simple present, not the future. So "who will score" becomes "who scores the maximum points".

◦ Correct: ... the player who scores the maximum points in the game will clinch the trophy this year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "who scores the points maximum" has wrong word order.

• Option 2 "who were score" and Option 3 "who have score" are grammatically incorrect verb forms.

NOTE

• Rule: In clauses beginning with "who/when/if/until/as soon as", we use the simple present to refer to the future — "The one who comes first will win" (not "will come").

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the challenges, / they ultimate achieved / their goal of launching / their startup.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. they ultimate achieved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A verb ("achieved") must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Ultimate" is an adjective; the correct adverb is "ultimately".

◦ Correct: ... they ultimately achieved their goal of launching their startup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Despite the challenges,", "their goal of launching" and "their startup" are all correct.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: an adjective describes a noun (the ultimate goal), while an adverb describes a verb (they ultimately achieved). Most adverbs of manner/degree end in "-ly".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word(s) in the given sentence.

Manik said that it is mandatory that each student pay his/her tuition fees every month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. each student pays.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "each" is always singular and takes a singular verb. In the simple present, a singular subject takes the verb with "-s" → "each student pays".

◦ Correct: ... it is mandatory that each student pays his/her tuition fees every month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "paids" is not a word.

• Option 3 "paid" is past tense (wrong tense for a general rule).

• Option 4 "each students pay" wrongly makes "student" plural after "each".

NOTE

• "Each / every / one of / either / neither + singular noun + singular verb": "Each boy has a pen", "Every student is present".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Once the seminar was over, the host gave up the certificates to the active participants.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. gave away.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "give away", meaning to distribute or hand out (something), especially prizes/certificates. "Give up" (to quit) is wrong in this context.

◦ Correct: ... the host gave away the certificates to the active participants.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "brought about" (cause to happen), Option 2 "came by" (obtained) and Option 4 "put across" (communicated) do not fit distributing certificates.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "give": give away (distribute/reveal), give up (quit), give in (surrender), give off (emit), give out (distribute / run out).

question:
Rectify the error in the given sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options provided.

The nights of King Arthur were known for their chivalry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. knights.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context of "King Arthur" and "chivalry" requires "knights" — medieval mounted warriors of noble rank — not "nights" (periods of darkness). They are homophones. (शूरवीर / योद्धा)

◦ Correct: The knights of King Arthur were known for their chivalry.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Night" (the time of darkness) and "knight" (a warrior) sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

• Options 2 "naughts" (zeros) and 3 "knots" (ties in a rope) are unrelated.

NOTE

• King Arthur's "Knights of the Round Table" are legendary. "Chivalry" refers to the medieval knightly code of honour, courage and courtesy.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

I want to buy the less expensive bike, but with the best mileage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. least.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" and the parallel superlative "the best mileage" indicate that the superlative degree is required — "the least expensive bike" (the cheapest of all).

◦ Correct: I want to buy the least expensive bike, but with the best mileage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "little" and Option 3 "lesser" are not superlatives.

• Option 4 "most less" is grammatically wrong (double form).

NOTE

• Degrees of "little/few (amount)": little – less – least. "The least expensive" = the cheapest. It parallels "the best mileage" (both superlatives with "the").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher asked us to __________ the main idea of the passage in the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. summarise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Summarise" means to give a brief statement of the main points of something. Capturing "the main idea of the passage" is exactly summarising. (सारांश देना)

◦ Correct: The teacher asked us to summarise the main idea of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "conclusion" is a noun, not a verb (it cannot follow "to").

• Option 3 "underestimate" (to value too low) and Option 4 "plagiarise" (to copy someone's work) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Summarise" (verb) / "summary" (noun). A good summary is brief, covers the main points, and is written in one's own words.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

The youngest employees / are chosen by the / organisation to / manage the fieldwork.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The youngest employees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The superlative "youngest" is used to single out one/the highest of a group, but the context here refers generally to a category of employees, so the positive degree "young" is appropriate — "The young employees are chosen ...".

◦ Correct: The young employees are chosen by the organisation to manage the fieldwork.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "are chosen by the", "organisation to" and "manage the fieldwork" are all correct (a proper passive structure).

NOTE

• Use the superlative ("youngest") only when comparing three or more and singling out the extreme one, usually with a defining phrase. For a general description, the positive degree ("young") is correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The most effective way to enhance your vocabulary is to look to unknown words in a dictionary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. look up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "look up", meaning to search for information (e.g., a word's meaning) in a dictionary or reference book. "Look to" is wrong here.

◦ Correct: ... the most effective way to enhance your vocabulary is to look up unknown words in a dictionary.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "write off" (to cancel/dismiss), Option 3 "set by" (not standard) and Option 4 "stand against" (to oppose) do not fit.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "look": look up (search for information / improve), look after (care for), look for (search), look into (investigate), look up to (admire).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

The thieves had no alternative / but to acquiesce with / the orders of / the police.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. but to acquiesce with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "acquiesce" (to accept or agree reluctantly) takes the preposition "in" or "to", not "with". So it should be "acquiesce in / to the orders".

◦ Correct: The thieves had no alternative but to acquiesce in the orders of the police.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The thieves had no alternative", "the orders of" and "the police" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Acquiesce" means to agree silently/reluctantly. Correct prepositions: acquiesce in a decision / acquiesce to a demand. Synonyms: comply, consent, submit, yield.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

The microscopic chip that emits a uniqe signal has been embedded into your arm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. uniqe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uniqe" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "unique", meaning being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else. (अद्वितीय / अनोखा)

◦ Example: Every fingerprint is unique.

• Spelling key: U + NI + QUE — it ends in "-que" (as in antique, technique, opaque).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Embedded", "emits" and "microscopic" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-que" (French origin): unique, antique, technique, boutique, opaque, plaque. The "-que" is pronounced like "k".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Benevolent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Kind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Benevolent" means well-meaning, kind and generous; wishing to do good to others. Its closest synonym is "kind". (परोपकारी / दयालु)

◦ Example: The benevolent/kind businessman donated to many charities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Enthusiastic" (eager), Option 3 "Mysterious" (puzzling) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Hostile" (unfriendly) is an antonym of benevolent.

NOTE

• Synonyms of benevolent: kind, kindly, generous, charitable, compassionate, humane.

• Antonyms: malevolent, cruel, unkind, hostile.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Careful
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cautious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Careful" means taking care to avoid harm or mistakes; attentive and watchful. Its closest synonym is "cautious" (careful to avoid danger). (सतर्क / सावधान)

◦ Example: Be careful/cautious while handling electrical equipment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Corrupt" (dishonest), Option 3 "Captivating" (charming) and Option 4 "Corrosive" (able to corrode) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of careful: cautious, attentive, prudent, watchful, vigilant, meticulous.

• Antonyms: careless, reckless, negligent, hasty.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Poonam used a rubber band to keep the pencils together. 'Band' here means __________.
option_1: a thin ring of rubber used for holding things together
option_2: a long rigid piece of wood or metal
option_4: a range of values or frequencies within a series
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a thin ring of rubber used for holding things together.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context "a rubber band to keep the pencils together", the word "band" means "a thin ring/loop (of rubber) used for holding things together". (रबर बैंड / छल्ला)

◦ Example: She tied the papers with a rubber band.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a long rigid piece of wood or metal" describes a rod/bar, not a band.

• Option 3 "a tube filled with water" is unrelated.

• Option 4 "a range of values or frequencies within a series" is the scientific/technical sense of "band" (e.g., a frequency band), which does not fit this context.

NOTE

• "Band" is a homonym with several meanings: a rubber band (a loop), a music band (a group), a frequency band (a range), a band/strip of colour. Context decides the meaning.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fulfeel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fulfeel" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Fulfil" (British) / "Fulfill" (American), meaning to carry out or achieve (a task, promise or desire). (पूरा करना)

◦ Example: He worked hard to fulfil his dream of becoming a pilot.

• Spelling key: FUL + FIL — note single "l" in "ful" and the ending "-fil" (British).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Altogether", "Always" and "Until" are all correctly spelt (note each has a single "l": altogether, always, until).

NOTE

• Related forms: fulfil (verb), fulfilment/fulfillment (noun), fulfilling (adjective). Watch the single/double "l": fulfil (UK) / fulfill (US).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

The partners ended up being traitorous to each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Faithful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Traitorous" means betraying trust; disloyal or treacherous. Its antonym is "faithful", meaning loyal and trustworthy. (विश्वासघाती का विलोम — वफादार)

◦ Example: A traitorous soldier betrayed his country, unlike the faithful ones who defended it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Disloyal" and Option 4 "Fickle" (changeable) are synonyms (or near) of traitorous.

• Option 2 "Proficient" (skilled) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of traitorous: treacherous, disloyal, unfaithful, perfidious.

• Antonyms: faithful, loyal, trustworthy, devoted.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who rules with absolute power and authority
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dictator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "dictator" is a ruler with total, absolute power over a country, typically one who has obtained it by force and governs oppressively. (तानाशाह / अधिनायक)

◦ Example: The country suffered under the rule of a cruel dictator.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Senator" — a member of a senate (legislature).

• Option 2 "Ruler" — a general term for one who rules (not necessarily absolute).

• Option 4 "Sovereign" — a supreme ruler/monarch (but not specifically one with oppressive absolute power).

NOTE

• "Dictator" implies absolute and often oppressive power. Related: dictatorship (rule by a dictator), autocrat, despot, tyrant.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

The entire audience was all ears when the Indian-born American economist started giving a speech.
option_2: was willing to exit the show
option_3: was arguing in favour of both sides
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. was keen to listen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to be all ears" means to be listening eagerly and attentively; keen to hear what someone has to say. (ध्यान से सुनने को उत्सुक)

◦ Example: Tell me your plan — I'm all ears.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eager to speak", Option 2 "willing to exit" and Option 3 "arguing in favour of both sides" do not convey attentive listening.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of attention: "lend an ear" (listen), "prick up one's ears" (start listening attentively), "hang on someone's every word".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is known for his humility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humility" means the quality of being humble; a modest view of one's own importance. Its antonym is "pride" (an excessively high opinion of oneself / arrogance). (विनम्रता का विलोम — घमंड)

◦ Example: Despite his success, he showed great humility, without a trace of pride.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Knowledge", Option 3 "Beauty" and Option 4 "Agility" (nimbleness) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of humility: modesty, humbleness, meekness.

• Antonyms: pride, arrogance, conceit, vanity, haughtiness.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Bheem has been shown in the popular culture as someone who eats in large quantity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. eats like a horse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to eat like a horse" means to eat a very large amount of food. It perfectly replaces "eats in large quantity". (बहुत अधिक खाना)

◦ Example: After the workout, he was so hungry that he ate like a horse.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eat humble pie" — to admit one's mistake humbly.

• Option 3 "eat like a bird" — to eat very little (the opposite).

• Option 4 "chews the fat" — to chat casually.

NOTE

• Contrasting idioms: "eat like a horse" (eat a lot) vs "eat like a bird" (eat very little). Bheem/Bhima from the Mahabharata is famed for his huge appetite.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Their" is the possessive determiner meaning "belonging to them" — the tails belong to the three rats. "a new use for their tails". (उनकी)

◦ Correct: Three big fat rats once found a new use for their tails.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "it's" = "it is" (a contraction, wrong here).

• Option 4 "there" refers to a place.

• Option 1 "the" would be grammatically weaker than the possessive "their".

NOTE

• Confusable words: their (possessive), there (place), they're (they are); its (possessive) vs it's (it is). Here the tails belong to the rats → "their".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. creeping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Creeping" means moving slowly, quietly and carefully (so as not to be noticed). Rats sneaking into a larder at night would be "creeping into" it. (धीरे-धीरे/चुपके से जाना)

◦ Correct: During the night, they came creeping into the larder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dreaming", Option 2 "acting" and Option 3 "yelling" (shouting) do not suit the stealthy, silent movement of rats at night.

NOTE

• "Creep – crept – crept" means to move slowly and quietly. Synonyms: sneak, tiptoe, slink, steal (in the sense of moving quietly).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. narrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The jar had a "narrow neck" — a small, thin opening — which is why the rats could not reach the treacle with their mouths or paws. This detail explains the problem. (सँकरा / तंग)

◦ Correct: But the jar had a narrow neck ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "funny", Option 3 "obese" (very fat — used for living beings, not a jar's neck) and Option 4 "slow" do not logically describe a jar's neck that blocks access.

NOTE

• "Narrow" = of small width. The narrow neck is the obstacle that makes the rats invent their clever tail-dipping trick. Antonym: wide/broad.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. struck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collocation "an idea struck someone" means an idea suddenly came to one's mind. So "a bright idea struck one of them". (एक विचार सूझना / मन में आना)

◦ Correct: At last, a bright idea struck one of them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flew", Option 2 "went" and Option 4 "stood" do not collocate with "idea" in this sense.

NOTE

• Collocations with "idea": an idea struck me / occurred to me / came to me / hit me. "Strike – struck – struck" here means to come suddenly to the mind.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "lick off" means to remove (something) by licking. The rats licked the treacle off the tail. (चाटकर हटाना / उतारना)

◦ Correct: ... allowed the two rats to lick it off.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "lick at" (to lick tentatively), "lick by" and "lick in" do not convey removing the treacle from the tail.

NOTE

• Phrasal verb "lick off" = to remove by licking. Similar: wipe off, brush off, wash off, rub off (all meaning to remove something from a surface).
